fatal_errors: The proposed hydrogen/pre-strain intervention does not reconstruct the AlCoCrFeNi coating and post-deposition annealing intervention.
The cited study supports hydrogen retention and reduced fracture energy in pre-strained 22K steel, but does not establish passive-film degradation or increased electrochemical corrosion.
The proposed material class excludes high-alloy stainless steels, whereas the target concerns coated SS316L.
explanation: The hypothesis is testable and broadly relevant to degradation of steels in hydrogen-bearing service, but it addresses hydrogen embrittlement in carbon or low-alloy steel rather than the target mechanism: corrosion protection of SS316L by an APS-deposited AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating annealed at 550 °C. It therefore misses the target materials, processing conditions, microstructural mediator, Al/Cr-rich passive products, and electrochemical and molten-salt outcomes. Its experiment includes useful hydrogen, mechanical, surface, and corrosion measurements and a clear falsification rule, although a complete factorial design with charged/un­charged and strained/unstrained controls would better separate hydrogen effects from direct pre-strain effects. Most importantly, E1 validates persistent trapped hydrogen and loss of fracture resistance, not the asserted causal chain from hydrogen trapping to oxide-film failure and corrosion acceleration.
